name: AirtableExists
title: Airtable Exists
description: Check whether a record with a given field value already exists in a table
whenToUse: Pick to answer "is this already in Airtable?" before writing: it looks for one record whose field equals a value and returns a boolean plus the record id. Use it as a guard on a branch; it checks one value rather than fetching rows.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Trigger. The field and value usually template from upstream output.

outputs.name: exists
outputs.description: Whether a matching record was found

outputs.name: recordId
outputs.description: The matching record's Airtable id, or null when there was no match

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.

package.name: airtable
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# FULLY DECLARATIVE. Three nodes, one base URL, one token.
#
# This package forced TWO executor capabilities, both loops a manifest cannot write itself:
# `paginate` for reading past the first page, and `chunk` for writing a collection when the
# vendor caps a batch at ten. Every list-returning and collection-writing node after this
# one inherits both.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/airtable/`.

name: airtable
displayName: Airtable
description: Read, check and write Airtable records
version: 2.0.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775377626/gravity/icons/airtable.png

features:
  - Fetch records with filters, views and sorting, paginated
  - Check whether a value already exists
  - Insert and update records, batched and deduplicated

allowedHosts:
  - api.airtable.com

requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [cursor]
  chunk: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.3.0"

credentials.airtableCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: airtableCredential
displayName: Airtable
description: Airtable Personal Access Token for reading and writing to Airtable bases
documentationUrl: https://airtable.com/create/tokens

properties:
  - name: personalAccessToken
    displayName: Personal Access Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Airtable Personal Access Token
    placeholder: pat

shared.rows.yaml:
# The row-splitting expressions, defined ONCE and $ref'd wherever they are needed.
#
# `AirtableInsert` needs "which rows are updates" and "which rows are creates" in three
# places each: the call's `when`, its `chunk.items`, and the skipped count in events. The
# sandbox has no assignment, so there is no way to bind an intermediate value inside an
# expression. A shared fragment is how one definition serves all three, and it is why these
# live here rather than being pasted six times.

# An Airtable record id is "rec" plus 14 characters. A row carrying one is an UPDATE.
isAirtableId: &isAirtableId >-
  return (config.records || []).filter(r =>
    typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec')

# Everything else is a CREATE. `id` is RESERVED by Airtable, so a row carrying its own
# non-Airtable `id` has it renamed to `apollo_id` rather than dropped: the retired code did
# this, and changing it would silently lose a column.
#
# Then anything the dedup field says is already in the table is removed. `calls.existing` is
# the paged read; when dedup is off that call is skipped and there is no key, so the filter
# passes everything through.
toCreate: &toCreate >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .map(r => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(r).map(e => [e[0] === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : e[0], e[1]])))
    .filter(r => !String(config.dedupField || '').trim()
      || !((calls.existing || {}).items || [])
           .map(x => String(((x.fields || {})[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField]) ?? ''))
           .filter(Boolean)
           .includes(String(r[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField] ?? '')))

# Offered minus kept: how many the dedup field dropped.
skipped: &skipped >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .length
  - (calls.creates ? calls.creates.sent : 0)

# The same set, as a boolean, for the call's `when`. Defined next to it so the two cannot
# drift: a `when` that disagreed with `items` would either skip a needed write or send an
# empty one.
toCreateAny: &toCreateAny >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .filter(r => !String(config.dedupField || '').trim()
      || !((calls.existing || {}).items || [])
           .map(x => String(((x.fields || {})[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField]) ?? ''))
           .filter(Boolean)
           .includes(String(r[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField] ?? '')))
    .length > 0
shared.table.yaml:
# Everything the three nodes share: the auth, and the url for one table.
#
# The table part may be a NAME ("Companies") or an id ("tbl..."), so it is percent-encoded.
# The base id never needs encoding.

credential: &credential
  scheme: bearer
  token: "{{ credentials.airtableCredential.personalAccessToken }}"

url: &url >-
  return 'https://api.airtable.com/v0/' + config.baseId
    + '/' + encodeURIComponent(config.tableId)

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: exists
  from: response
  value: "return (response.records || []).length > 0"

- emit: recordId
  from: response
  value: "return ((response.records || [])[0] || {}).id || null"
files.api/run.yaml:
# One record is enough to answer the question, so maxRecords is 1 and there is no paging.
#
# The formula is a string the vendor parses, so the value is escaped. Double quotes are the
# only delimiter that needs it here, and split/join does it without a regex, which the
# expression sandbox does not allow.

- name: match
  method: GET
  url: { $ref: table#url }
  credential: { $ref: table#credential }
  query:
    filterByFormula: >-
      return '{' + config.field + '}="'
        + String(config.value).split('"').join('\\"')
        + '"'
    maxRecords: "1"
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [baseId, tableId, field, value]
  properties:
    baseId:
      type: string
      title: Base ID
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    tableId:
      type: string
      title: Table Name or ID
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    field:
      type: string
      title: Field Name
      description: The field to match on
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    value:
      type: string
      title: Value
      description: The value to look for
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order": [authRequired, authRole, baseId, tableId, field, value]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Trigger. The field and value usually template from upstream output.

outputs:
  - name: exists
    type: boolean
    description: Whether a matching record was found
  - name: recordId
    type: string
    description: The matching record's Airtable id, or null when there was no match

credentials:
  - name: airtableCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Airtable
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: AirtableExists
kind: PromiseNode
name: Airtable Exists
category: Storage & Data
color: "#FCB400"
description: Check whether a record with a given field value already exists in a table
whenToUse: >
  Pick to answer "is this already in Airtable?" before writing: it looks for one record
  whose field equals a value and returns a boolean plus the record id. Use it as a guard on
  a branch; it checks one value rather than fetching rows.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# Needs a real base. A MISS is a valid result, so this asserts the shape rather than a hit.
testData:
  config:
    baseId: appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
    tableId: Companies
    field: Name
    value: A Company That Does Not Exist
  inputs:
    input: {}
  expect:
    exists: "return typeof output.exists === 'boolean'"
    recordId: "return output.exists ? typeof output.recordId === 'string' : output.recordId === null"
